title: Dulcha Singh Urges Delay While Others Boast of Easy Victory

blocks.text: This page contrasts empty bravado with sober military judgment. Those who had never seen the Singhs fighting a battle talk loosely of loot, horses, and easy fame, as though the Majhail veterans before them were an ordinary enemy.

On the Khalsa side, however, the scale of the Malwa preparations causes unease, and practical men begin sending valuables away before the fighting closes in. Dulcha Singh argues that Now he must keep patience for five ten days, holding position and thinking carefully rather than letting pride force a rash move.

The page therefore prepares the larger confrontation by showing two mentalities at once. One side mistakes noise for victory, while the other measures risk, supply, and reputation before committing fully.
